back: A mixture of a metal with other elements.
notes: Its composition can vary, because it is a mixture.

back: Copper + zinc. Musical instruments, door handles, plug pins (hard, resists corrosion).
Copper + tin. Statues, medals, bells (hard, resists corrosion).
Iron with a small amount of carbon: strong and hard.
Iron with chromium, nickel and carbon. Cutlery: hard and resists rusting.
Aluminium with copper (and a little magnesium and manganese). Aircraft bodies: light and strong.

front: Why are alloys harder than pure metals (Supplement)?
back: Atoms of different sizes disrupt the layers, so the layers cannot slide over each other easily.

front: What does an alloy look like in a particle diagram?
back: A regular arrangement of metal atoms with some atoms of a different size mixed among them.

front: Why are alloys more useful than pure metals?
back: They can be harder and stronger, and some resist corrosion better.
An alloy of iron and chromium made from chromite ore; used to make stainless steel.
